title: Keep impossible page requests out of the listing service

blocks.text: The listing service pages through products with a `PageRequest(int page, int size)`. Requests come from query parameters, from saved searches (which store only the page), and from `next()` when a client scrolls on. The database has started receiving `OFFSET -2147483648`, and a client that asks for `size=5000` gets a page of 5,000 rows, which the service then caches under a key that no request at the limit ever hits.

items: the compact constructor: no request may exist with a page below 0 or a size below 1 (refuse them with `IllegalArgumentException`), and a size above `MAX_SIZE` is served as `MAX_SIZE`;
`fromQuery(page, size)`: reads the two query parameters; without a size the client gets `DEFAULT_SIZE`.

blocks.text: When you're done, an impossible request can't be made by any route, and a request for more than `MAX_SIZE` rows is the same request as one for exactly `MAX_SIZE`. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: query parameters become a request with that page and size, the default size when size is absent, and next() steps one page on
a query with a negative page or a size below 1 is refused with IllegalArgumentException
a negative page or a size below 1 is refused however the request is made: the one-argument constructor, the canonical one, or next() past the last int
a request above the size limit is equal to, hashes like and is found in a set as the request at the limit

origin.section: A Custom Constructor Must Call the Canonical One First, So Checks Belong in the Canonical One

concepts: Every other constructor must start with this(...), so every way of making a record ends in the canonical constructor, and a check placed anywhere else guards only one path.
A value assigned to a parameter in the compact constructor is the value stored, so equals, hashCode and the accessor all see it.
